image_description: A close-up view of a vehicle wheel assembly, specifically focusing on the braking system. The image shows a rusty, solid metal disc (rotor) mounted to a hub with lug nuts. A teal/green painted caliper housing is visible at the top left, clamping onto the rotor. There is a distinct blue ring or marking on the outer edge of the rotor face. The surrounding area includes suspension components and a tire sidewall.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Circular metal rotor (disc), notably larger in diameter than its thickness.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The rotor is clearly circular and its diameter significantly exceeds its thickness, matching the geometric description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Caliper is cast metal mounted over rotor edge.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A teal-colored caliper assembly is visible straddling the upper portion of the rotor.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Rotor is mounted to wheel hub with visible lug bolt pattern.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Five lug nuts/bolts are clearly visible securing the rotor to the central hub.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Rotor is ventilated (two plates with cooling fins) or solid.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The rotor appears to be a solid disc type; while internal ventilation isn't explicitly visible from this angle, it fits the 'solid' criteria of the checkpoint.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Brake pads are rectangular friction material blocks pressing against rotor faces.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The brake pads are housed inside the caliper and are not directly visible from this external angle.
Dark tubing/lines are visible connecting to the rear/top of the caliper assembly.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Surface shows machined concentric grooves or cross-drilled holes.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The rotor surface appears smooth with some rust and wear, but lacks distinct machined concentric grooves or cross-drilled holes typical of performance brakes.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Surface exhibits heat discoloration (blue/brown tint) from use.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: There is significant brown/orange rust and discoloration on the rotor surface, consistent with use and exposure.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Caliper is cast aluminum or iron.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The caliper has the textured appearance of cast metal, painted teal.

artifact_observations.reasoning: A bright blue ring on the friction surface of a brake rotor is physically unusual for standard operation (could be paint marker or AI hallucination of a highlight). It looks slightly unnatural compared to the rest of the rusty texture.
The connection between the teal caliper body and the mounting hardware is somewhat indistinct and muddy, lacking clear mechanical definition.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific class identity and distinguish from drum brakes or other wheel components.
To verify the caliper is correctly positioned over the rotor edge and not floating or merged incorrectly.
To assess the realism of the rust textures and the anomalous blue ring.

focus_areas: Mechanical connectivity between caliper and rotor
Realism of the blue ring artifact on the rotor surface
Texture consistency of rust vs. painted surfaces
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the blue ring on the rotor. Is this a plausible mechanic's mark (e.g., torque seal or runout gauge mark) or an AI color bleeding artifact? Evaluate if the rust texture looks procedurally generated or naturally corroded.
